data.name: Parkinson's disease
data.description: Neurodegenerative disease marked by loss of dopaminergic neurons and accumulation of misfolded alpha-synuclein (Lewy bodies). The relationship to mTOR is not settled in one direction. The study held here reports the opposite of the autophagy-failure account: chronic integrated-stress-response/ATF4 signalling suppresses both mTORC1 and mTORC2, and that sustained mTOR inhibition drives dopaminergic neuron death via PUMA (DEMMINGS2026). The familiar reading - that mTORC1 hyperactivity blocks alpha-synuclein clearance and that rapamycin enhances it in animal models - rests on work outside this corpus and is not graded here.
data.description_beginner: A brain disease caused by loss of dopamine-producing neurons and buildup of a misfolded protein (alpha-synuclein) into Lewy bodies. Which way mTOR points here is genuinely unsettled. The usual story is that too much mTOR blocks the cleanup that would clear the protein. The one study in this Atlas says close to the opposite: too LITTLE mTOR signalling, held down for a long time, is what kills the neurons.

studies.title: ATF4 activates a transcriptional program that chronically suppresses mTOR activity and promotes neurodegeneration in Parkinson disease models
studies.authors: Demmings MD; Kane EA; Tennyson EC; Hurley K; Zhao J; Cruickshanks NA; Ciz V; Krupa JM; Pasternak SH; Cregan SP

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse (neurotoxin and alpha-synucleinopathy PD models) and cultured neurons
studies.finding: Chronic integrated-stress-response signalling through ATF4 coordinately upregulates SESN2, DDIT4 and Trib3, which together suppress BOTH mTORC1 and mTORC2; this sustained mTOR inhibition drives dopaminergic neuron death via the pro-apoptotic BCL-2 family protein PUMA. Defines a maladaptive ISR/ATF4-to-mTOR axis in Parkinson disease models — a case where LESS mTOR activity is harmful, opposite to the usual longevity framing.
